## Fatal finding

### `def-subobject-and-quotient-object`, propagated into `thm-subobjects-and-quotient-objects-form-oppositely-ordered-collections` and `def-well-powered-and-co-well-powered-category`

- **Locations:** [Definition of subobject classes](/Users/ianx/Projects/prestige-math-library/items/def-subobject-and-quotient-object.md:28), [ordered-collection Statement and `[L2]`](/Users/ianx/Projects/prestige-math-library/items/thm-subobjects-and-quotient-objects-form-oppositely-ordered-collections.md:26), and [well-poweredness Definition](/Users/ianx/Projects/prestige-math-library/items/def-well-powered-and-co-well-powered-category.md:27).
- **What is wrong:** The text treats equivalence classes drawn from a proper class of monomorphisms as entities that form a further “collection,” possibly a set. That is unavailable under the repository’s stated ZFC convention, where a class is a formula, “not an additional set” ([class convention](/Users/ianx/Projects/prestige-math-library/items/rem-category-theory-class-and-size-conventions.md:25)). No universe, Scott-class coding, or representative encoding is supplied.
- **Counterexample:** Take the definable chaotic groupoid whose objects are all ordinals and with exactly one morphism between every ordered pair. It is locally small, and every morphism is an isomorphism and hence monic. For any fixed ordinal \(C\), all morphisms \(\alpha\to C\) mutually factor, so there is informally one subobject—but its literal equivalence class contains one morphism for every ordinal and is therefore a proper class. Nevertheless \(\{1_C\}\) is a set-indexed representative family, uniformly for every \(C\), so the “supplied well-powering” of line 29 exists. Thus lines 27 and 29 do not describe the intended ordinary/supplied versions coherently when “subobject” literally means the equivalence class defined upstream.
- **Additional dependency mismatch:** `[L2]` applies `def-partial-order` to these possibly proper collections, but the cited definition explicitly begins “Let \(P\) be a set” ([dependency text](/Users/ianx/Projects/prestige-math-library/items/def-partial-order.md:38)). The Statement explicitly declines to assume well-poweredness, so the cited item has a changed domain.
- **Severity:** **fatal** — missing size/class encoding in Definitions and a Statement-level domain mismatch.

No other defect was found in the assigned items.

Boundary checks passed: empty categories where meaningful; empty diagrams for limits, colimits, and completeness; empty and singleton subobject families; zero objects; empty separating families; and both directions of the two iff results. No assigned item targets an `ai-generated` Statement or Construction through `deps`.

Coverage: I read all 16 assigned items fully, all ten corresponding proof-contract entries including every boundary row, and all 18 distinct direct dependency items fully. I also read the class-size convention and the relevant large-category counterexample fully. The batch reader/Alpha records and batch notes were sampled only to verify current disk state. Nothing required by the dispatch remained unchecked.
